routes.title: From the room to the grave
routes.dek: The order of a death as people handled it: the threshold, the body, the rite, then the ground.

steps.why: The body as something that has to be handled.
The rite that follows, with its scheme and its misattributions.
Where the dead are put, and who decides.
How the state took over the funeral and what remains of it.

routes.title: Outside the churchyard
routes.dek: Places where the sources put the dead who were not laid in the usual ground. Each plate says how thin its evidence is.

steps.why: The returning dead and the argument about who counts as one.
Reports of burial in forest ravines, with their provenance, and one traveller’s photograph of old graves.
Water and the calendar day for the drowned.
Crossroads, and a modern count of roadside memorials.

routes.title: What the record cannot hold
routes.dek: Plates that are mostly about the limits of their own evidence.

steps.why: The plate that is empty on purpose.
A rite that concerns houses and a census that counts villages.
A flooded town and a claim about cemeteries that stays unverified.
Mass death and the gap between the record and the official number.

routes.title: Images of the dead
routes.dek: How death was painted, printed and photographed.

steps.why: The Last Judgment as a picture to be read.
Russian painting and the dead body.
Memorial architecture and the photographs left by the Soviet funeral.
The laments and the address to the dead.
Back to the rite that frames both.
